title: Technical interview preparation
audience: a computer science graduate or an experienced self-taught programmer preparing for and starting a software engineering job
purpose: Prepare for software engineering interviews: how the process works, problem-solving patterns (arrays and hashing, two pointers, sliding windows, stacks, binary search, linked lists, trees, graphs, heaps, intervals, backtracking and dynamic programming), explaining your approach and its complexity while you code, behavioral interviews, résumés and offers.

weeks.1: The interview process and how to practice
weeks.8: Graphs: BFS, DFS and topological sort

blocks.deliverable: Solve eight problems with these patterns.
Week 7 midterm; a timed mock interview of two problems.
Write five STAR stories and a one-page résumé.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Interview readiness: complete a timed mock interview loop (two supplied coding problems, a system-design sketch and a behavioral interview), self-grade with the supplied rubrics, keep a pattern log of 60 solved problems, and write a final résumé and study plan.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
